diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $c$ be a cost function such that for all particle $i$, $c_i : y\in \Omega \mapsto c(y,\bm{x}_i)\in [0,+\infty) $ belongs to $C^{1,1}(\Omega)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem claims unique weights, a unique T, and zero-measure intersections under only C^{1,1}. But the Laguerre cells depend only on differences c_i-w_i, so adding a constant to all w_i leaves every cell unchanged; weights are not unique. More seriously, C^{1,1} does not prevent two cost functions from coinciding on a positive-measure set. If c_i=c_j on a set of positive measure and v_i,v_j>0, the cells defined by the displayed inequalities either overlap on that set or force one cell empty; no weights give disjoint cells with volumes v_i,v_j, and the optimal map is not unique. Thus the stated uniqueness and zero-measure intersection fail without a non-degeneracy/tie-breaking assumption.

failure_location.quote: The intersection of two Laguerre cells has zero Lebesgue measure and the weights $w_i\in \mathbb{R}$, called Kantorovich potentials, are uniquely defined such that for all $i\in\{1,\ldots,N\},$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a non-degeneracy/twist condition (ties have zero Lebesgue measure) and fix the additive normalization of the weights, or define an explicit tie-breaking rule.
issues.overall_effect: The foundational guarantee of a unique Laguerre tessellation and unique Kantorovich potentials is unreliable in degenerate cases; prose claims of a unique partition for any configuration inherit this gap.
issues.title: Theorem thm:semidiscrete overstates uniqueness and zero-measure intersections
issues.why_classification: The theorem is central, but the failure is a missing standard non-degeneracy condition and normalization; for the generic costs used in the paper the conclusion is recoverable without changing the method.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $c$ be a cost function such that for all particle $i$, $c_i : y\in \Omega \mapsto c(y,\bm{x}_i)\in [0,+\infty) $ belongs to $C^{1,1}(\Omega)$.
For $\alpha=0.75$, large deformations lead to more elongated and non-convex shapes (left).

issues.failure_explanation: The cited theorem requires each cost c_i to be C^{1,1} on Omega. The paper uses power costs |x-x_i|^alpha with alpha<1 (e.g. alpha=0.5,0.75) and periodized distances. For alpha<1 the cost is not C^1 at x=x_i, and centroids generally lie in Omega; the periodized distance also has derivative discontinuities. Hence the theorem's existence/uniqueness guarantee does not apply to these advertised soft-particle and periodic examples as written.

failure_location.quote: a power cost $c(\bm{x},\bm{x}_i) = |\bm{x}-\bm{x}_i|^{\alpha_i}$ where the $\alpha_i$ are distributed uniformly between 0.5 and 4.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Extend the theorem to the used cost classes or add a separate argument handling the measure-zero singularities and periodized distance.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical guarantee of a unique Laguerre tessellation for soft particles with alpha<1 and for periodic domains is unsupported by the cited theorem.
issues.title: Central theorem applied to costs outside its C^{1,1} hypothesis
issues.why_classification: The guarantee is unavailable for a whole advertised softness regime and periodic examples; repairing it requires extending or replacing the invoked result, though the numerical method may still work.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then let $\mathscr{S}\subset\Omega$ be any shape of volume $v_i$.
there exists a unique $w^*>0$ such that $U(w^*) = v_i$.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma statement omits the volume constraint |S|=v_i, which the proof uses. Without it, the minimizer is the empty set, not a positive-level set. Even with the volume constraint, the proof assumes U(w)=|{c<=w}| is continuous and strictly increasing enough to take the value v_i. A C^{1,1} cost can have a positive-measure level set (e.g. c=0), so no level set of volume v_i need exist and the minimizer need not be a single sublevel set.

failure_location.quote:
The shape $\mathscr{S}\subset\Omega$ that minimizes the individual energy 
\[\mathcal{I}(\mathscr{S}) = \int_{\mathscr{S}} c(\bm{x},\bm{x}_i)\dd \bm{x}\]
is of the form 
\[\mathscr{S}(w) = \{\bm{x}\in\Omega,\,\, c(\bm{x},\bm{x}_i) \leq w\},\]
for some $w>0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State |S|=v_i and add a non-degeneracy assumption such as level sets having zero measure and U continuous, or allow a subset of a level set.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that individual shapes are always level sets of the cost and that any shape can be realized as such is not justified for flat or degenerate costs.
issues.title: Preferred-shape lemma omits volume constraint and level-set continuity
issues.why_classification: The missing volume constraint is contextually clear and the flat-level-set issue is a standard non-degeneracy condition; the costs used in the paper survive the repair.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: A drawback of our discretization procedure is that there is generally no Monge map between two discrete measures.

issues.failure_explanation: The discrete OT problem between pixels and particles generally has no Monge map; its optimal plan can split the mass of a pixel among several particles. The proposed argmin map assigns each pixel wholly to one particle, so the resulting cell volumes are the counts of assigned pixels divided by M and need not equal the prescribed volumes v_i. The Sinkhorn potentials w_i enforce the marginals of the soft transport plan, not of this hard assignment. Thus the discrete construction does not inherit the exact volume constraint of the continuous Monge map.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the transport plan with mass splitting, solve for weights so the hard assignment volumes match v_i when possible, or explicitly state and accept approximate volumes.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical method's advertised strict volume preservation is not guaranteed by the stated discrete allocation map; computed cell volumes may differ from v_i.
issues.title: Discrete allocation map does not guarantee prescribed volumes
issues.why_classification: The strict volume guarantee is compromised in the discrete implementation; a contained algorithmic change is needed to restore it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The position $\bm{x}_i$ of a particle $i$ should be understood as a positional indication but as we shall see later, it does not necessarily correspond to the barycenter of the set $\mathscr{S}_i$.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed quantity is the second moment of the cell points about x_i, not their empirical covariance. The covariance matrix requires centering at the sample mean \bar y_i = (1/N_i) sum_{y in L_i} y. Since the paper explicitly states that x_i need not be the barycenter of the cell, the principal eigenvector of this matrix can be biased and is not generally the cell's orientation covariance.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace x_i by the sample mean of the cell points in the covariance formula.
issues.overall_effect: The collision-induced orientation dynamics may use a misdefined covariance, affecting the claimed alignment mechanism.
issues.title: Empirical covariance formula is not centered at the sample mean
issues.why_classification: A local definition correction preserves the orientation method.

issues.failure_explanation: With phi=-log c, the shape is {c<=w}={phi>=-log w}. Favoring deformation in a direction requires lowering the cost c there, i.e. increasing phi. The choice f=-delta_+ lowers phi in the positive-gradient direction, thereby increasing c and penalizing that direction; it opposes the claimed elongation. The same sign inconsistency occurs in the random-protrusion perturbation f=-sum xi_k G, which would penalize rather than favor protrusions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the sign of f or define phi=+log c so that the stated perturbations favor the intended deformations.
issues.overall_effect: The chemotaxis and random-protrusion dynamics as written do not produce the claimed directed deformations; the sign of the perturbation must be reversed.
issues.title: Sign inversion in logarithmic cost perturbations
issues.why_classification: A local sign flip restores the claimed behavior.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The total force applied on $\bm{x}_i$ is thus equal to $\bm{\vec{F}}_{j\to i} + \bm{\vec{F}}_{0\to i}$

issues.failure_explanation: The force balance in the proof gives gamma_ij = 2 gamma_0 cos theta, so a contact angle exists only if gamma_ij <= 2 gamma_0. If gamma_ij > 2 gamma_0, no such theta solves the equation and the equilibrium is separated rather than a two-cap doublet. The lemma does not state this necessary condition, although the paper's separation regime uses exactly gamma_ij > gamma_bw + gamma_ow (which for identical particles is gamma_ij > 2 gamma_0).

failure_location.quote:
The equilibrium configuration, shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:doublet}, is made of two spherical caps with contact angle $\theta$ which satisfies 
\[\cos\theta = \frac{\gamma_{ij}}{2\gamma_0}.\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis gamma_ij <= 2 gamma_0 (or restrict the lemma to adhering doublets).
issues.overall_effect: The doublet equilibrium claim is invalid in the separation regime unless the missing condition is added.
issues.title: Cell-doublet lemma omits the condition gamma_ij <= 2 gamma_0
issues.why_classification: A missing boundary condition; adding it is local and preserves the lemma for the intended contact regime.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Homophilic sorting with internalization of one of the population.

issues.failure_explanation: Substituting the listed parameters gives 5 < 7-30 = -23, which is false. The condition has the sign of the medium-tension difference reversed; the shown internalization corresponds to gamma_bo < gamma_ow - gamma_bw (5 < 30-7). Thus the caption does not correctly state the condition it claims to validate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the inequality to gamma_bo < gamma_ow - gamma_bw (or an equivalent correct condition).
issues.overall_effect: The stated condition for homophilic internalization is unreliable; the figure's validation of that condition is misstated.
issues.title: Internalization condition in surface-tension caption has reversed sign
issues.why_classification: A one-line inequality correction restores the intended condition.
